summary: Oxford County, ME tower at Sabattus Mountain in Lovell, dated 1939; taken down in 1962 and moved to Mount Hope near Sanford, where a 2021 article says it still stands.

notes_for_editor: Dates rest on the Sun Journal table (1939 date; disassembled 1962 and moved to Mount Hope). The CCC link is Bill Cobb's statement in a 2021 Sun Journal feature, not a build record. The FFLA Maine chapter state listing table (last update 12/30/2021) gives Sabattus Mt., Lovell, Oxford, elevation 1280 ft, a 60 ft tower installed 1939, and the 1962 move; I could not identify its page URL, so it is not cited. Only the Sun Journal table links Sabattus to Mount Hope. The NHLR Mount Hope entry does not mention Sabattus (checked against the full cached page text); that negative claim has no quote to cite, so a second source for the move would strengthen the story. No staffing, access or fire data for the original Lovell site appears in any source read. The 2021 Sun Journal feature names Mount Hope as still standing and used to spot fires, and says the remaining standing towers are closed to the public, but it places Mount Hope in neither its open nor its closed group. The story therefore dates Mount Hope's status to 2021 and does not state its access. The NHLR entry gives staffing by volunteers but no access information.
